comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support claims C5, C18-C20, C27-C28, and C90 regarding the coccinella system's architecture, cost, and accessibility. Reviewers explicitly affirm the inexpensive hardware and open-source nature that OpenEval documents.

Strong agreement. Both support claims C40-C47 presenting quantitative results from the pharmacological screen. OpenEval also includes dose-response claims C50-C51, which peer reviewers implicitly accept as evidence of biological validity without explicit challenge.

Agreement on dose-response relationship (C50-C51). OpenEval treats this as separate validation evidence, while peer reviewers accept it within the broader pharmacological results as supporting biological validity.

Agreement on genetic validation (C52-C56). Both support the use of drug-resistant mutants to demonstrate biological specificity. OpenEval notes some speculation in C56, while peer reviewers accept the overall evidence as solid without specific concerns.

Agreement on high-throughput capability (C57-C61). Both support the large-scale validation results. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the system's ability to analyze hundreds of flies and its utility for gross locomotor defects.

Agreement on comparative analysis (C62-C70). Both support the comparison with high-resolution methods showing coccinella's performance. OpenEval also includes claims C6, C21, C72 about overall conclusions and limitations, which peer reviewers acknowledge by noting the trade-off between speed and information loss.

Agreement on main conclusions (C6, C21, C67, C72). Both support coccinella's comparative performance while acknowledging limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly note the system performs well for its intended use cases but has trade-offs.

Strong agreement on sleep deprivation experiments (C76-C80). Both support the validation approach where baseline discrimination failure rules out overfitting while rebound clustering demonstrates biological sensitivity. Peer reviewers affirm this shows the system is 'not simply overfitting data.'

Agreement on sleep threshold validation (C81-C85). Both support the detection of the 300s threshold as evidence of biological validity. OpenEval emphasizes this as key validation; peer reviewers accept it within the broader sleep analysis results.

Agreement on scope and intended use (C91, C95-C97, C99). Both accept coccinella as complementary to high-resolution methods, appropriate for drug screens and gross locomotor analysis but not for subtle behavioral modifications.

Partial agreement on technical specifications (C30-C36). OpenEval supports all technical details including maximal velocity choice. Peer reviewers accept the approach but request more explanation of HCTSA methodology, suggesting some uncertainty about the analytical framework.

Divergent evaluation on HCTSA pipeline (C37-C38, C128-C130). OpenEval finds the methodology well-documented and supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting the manuscript 'does not provide much explanation' and requesting more detail to make the method 'more convincing.'

Agreement on temporal resolution trade-offs (C29, C92-C94). Both acknowledge the system's limitations in temporal resolution. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'the rapidity of the platform comes at a cost--loss of information on subtle but important behavioral alterations.'
